claim.note: Heading level wrong: its siblings 4.3.8.3 Function-Identifier, 4.3.8.4 Reference Modification and 4.3.8.5 Identifier (page 169) are level-4 (####), and the parent 4.3.8 Uniqueness of Reference is level 3 (###); this subsection is emitted at the parent's level, so the outline makes Condition-Name a sibling of 4.3.8 rather than a child. (The renumbering to 4.3.8.6 is the marked Amendment 1 correction C94 and is not the finding.)
claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) breaks the document outline that section lookups and citation checks navigate by; the clause becomes unfindable by its number or is filed under the wrong parent.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 170 (folio IV-24) shows the subsection heading '4.3.8.5 Condition-Name' (renumbered 4.3.8.6 by Amendment 1, C94, which the markdown marks). In the transcription it is '### 4.3.8.6 Condition-Name'. specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 6872 is '### 4.3.8 Uniqueness of Reference', and the siblings are '#### 4.3.8.3 Function-Identifier' (line 7072), '#### 4.3.8.4 Reference Modification' (line 7109) and '#### 4.3.8.5 Identifier' (page-169.md line 31). So the outline makes the fifth-level clause 4.3.8.6 a peer of its parent 4.3.8. The number and title are correct; only the heading level is wrong. The defect is real and structural. The kind 'missing-heading' is imprecise, because the heading is present at the wrong level. Sibling note outside this claim: '### 4.3.8.1 Qualification' (line 6892) has the same wrong level, and 4.3.8.2 Subscripting (line 7006) has no markdown heading marker at all.
verdict.corrected_description: Heading level defect, not a missing heading. The clause heading is transcribed as '### 4.3.8.6 Condition-Name', level 3, the same level as its parent '### 4.3.8 Uniqueness of Reference'. It should be '#### 4.3.8.6 Condition-Name', level 4, matching its siblings 4.3.8.3, 4.3.8.4 and 4.3.8.5. The number and title are correct after the marked C94 renumbering.
